items.title: Spain Receives Record 908,288 Migrant Regularization Applications
items.body: The Spanish government has received 908,288 applications for its extraordinary migrant regularization program, surpassing initial projections of 750,000. Authorities have admitted 359,255 applications for processing so far, with two weeks remaining until the deadline. The record volume stems from more flexible requirements, including vulnerability reports and family unity criteria, though hundreds of applicants report significant processing delays.

items.title: Madrid Restricts Public Transport Pass to Registered Residents
items.body: The Community of Madrid now limits public transport passes exclusively to individuals with empadronamiento (municipal registration) in the region. This policy disproportionately affects foreign residents and migrants, as landlords frequently refuse to register tenants. Advocacy groups warn that the measure severely restricts affordable transit access for undocumented individuals, students, and workers from other regions.

items.title: U.S. and Iran Finalize Peace Deal, Reopening Strait of Hormuz
items.body: The United States and Iran finalized a provisional peace agreement that immediately lifts the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and resumes maritime traffic. While the deal caused oil prices to drop and pushed the Ibex 35 past 19,000 points, experts warn that lower energy costs will take months to reach consumers. Damaged infrastructure and logistical bottlenecks will delay the full transmission of reduced gas and oil prices to household budgets.

items.title: Doctors Threaten Indefinite Strike Starting in September
items.body: Medical professionals in Spain announced plans for an indefinite strike beginning in September if negotiations with the Ministry of Health stall. The doctors' committee rejected the professional framework, or Estatuto Marco, that the government approved with other unions earlier this month. A summer truce will pause the current conflict, but the escalation threatens to disrupt healthcare services nationwide.

items.title: Renewable Energy Cuts Monthly Electricity Bills by €10
items.body: Renewable energy sources saved Spanish households an average of €10 per month on electricity bills during the recent energy crisis. Gas sets the wholesale electricity price only 9% of the time, significantly reducing the impact of the 75% spike in gas prices during the Hormuz conflict. Although gas prices have dropped 10% following the peace deal, they remain 46% above pre-war levels, making the renewable buffer crucial for household budgets.

items.title: High Housing Prices Trigger Market Slowdown in Major Cities
items.body: Housing prices across Spain rose 12.9% in the first quarter of 2026, but buyer resistance is now cooling the market. Economist Gonzalo Bernardos notes that upper-middle-class demand in Madrid, Barcelona, and Valencia is rejecting current valuations, leading to a deceleration in housing investments. This pushback signals a potential shift in affordability dynamics for those looking to buy property in major urban centers.

items.title: High Rent Burdens Drive Mental Health Crisis Among Youth
items.body: A new report by Oxfam and youth organizations links the struggle to pay rent directly to deteriorating mental health among young people in Spain. The study finds that 62.7% of youth face housing access difficulties, with spending more than 30% to 50% of income on rent significantly increasing psychological distress. Researchers urge policymakers to address these socioeconomic factors to protect public well-being.

items.title: Solidarity Pension Contribution from High Salaries Surges 42%
items.body: The solidarity quota applied to high salaries will generate €567 million in pension contributions this year, marking a 42% increase from 2025. The Social Security Ministry implemented the measure last year as part of broader pension reforms to ensure the system's long-term viability. High-earning residents will see this increased social security deduction reflected in their net monthly income.

items.title: Domestic Flight Prices in Spain Surge by Record 25.6%
items.body: The cost of domestic flights in Spain jumped 25.6% in May, marking the largest monthly increase on record. International airfares also rose 2.5%, pushing the overall average ticket price up 8.9%. The surge stems from a 6.44% increase in Aena airport fees and elevated operational costs driven by higher oil prices during the recent geopolitical conflict.
